name: Graham Healthcare Group
desc:
Hospice Insurance Verification & Authorization Coordinator | $20 to $23/hr | Insurance Verification and Data Entry, Some Phone Calls, No Sales Expectations
Company: Graham Healthcare Group
Industry: Health Science

What Your Day Will Look Like:
Graham Healthcare Group runs home health and hospice care companies. In this role, you make sure a patient's insurance is checked and approved before nurses and other clinical staff start care. You'll work from a task list in Homecare Homebase (HCHB), the medical records system, and use insurance websites, phone, and fax to confirm benefits like deductibles, copays, and out-of-pocket costs. You'll get prior authorizations from insurance companies, send clinical information when they ask for it, and let the clinical team know about approvals and denials. You'll recheck Medicare, Medicaid, and other insurance every month to catch changes, and help the scheduling and billing teams fix insurance problems before they hold up visits or claims.

Soft Skills
- Attention to detail
- Patience and flexibility
- Critical thinking
- Clear communication with insurance companies and staff
- Working independently
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements

Education Minimum: Not required. An associate degree or a mix of experience and business courses is preferred.
Required Experience: Homecare Homebase (HCHB) experience, plus at least 1 year in insurance verification, authorization, or medical billing
Preferred Experience: Associate degree or business courses

Required Skills:
- Knowledge of Medicare, Medicaid, and private insurance authorization rules
- Comfortable using insurance company websites
- Microsoft Office
- Strong attention to detail
- Clear written and verbal communication
- Works well alone and with a team
- Must live in the Eastern or Central time zone
- Available every other Saturday, plus weekends, holidays, or after hours as needed

This role is ideal for someone who:
- Has worked in Homecare Homebase at a home health or hospice agency
- Has a year or more of insurance verification or medical billing
- Likes detail work and solving insurance problems
- Wants a full-time remote job with a pension and 15 days of PTO

Not a Good Fit for someone who:
- Has never used Homecare Homebase
- Has no insurance verification or medical billing experience
- Can't work every other Saturday
- Can't pass a drug screen that includes marijuana
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process:
1. Submit application
2. Expect an assessment email
3. Watch for an email inviting you to a prescreening
4. Depending on how well the prescreening went, expect an email to schedule an interview
This is an estimated process. A drug screen is part of the background check before you start.

Top 10 Resume Keywords
- Insurance verification
- Prior authorization
- Homecare Homebase (HCHB)
- Medicare and Medicaid
- Benefits verification
- Payer portals
- Hospice and home health
- Medical billing
- Eligibility review
- Documentation accuracy

4-5 Interview Questions for this Role:
- Tell us about your experience with Homecare Homebase.
- How do you verify a patient's benefits, and what details do you document?
- An insurance company denies an authorization. What are your next steps?
- Tell us about a time you caught an insurance error before it caused a problem. What happened, what did you do, and what was the result?
- Tell us about a time you worked with another team to fix a billing or scheduling issue. What was the problem, what did you do, and how did it turn out?
other:
Pay, Shift, Benefits, Background, Drug Test Information, and Career Pathway:
-Pay: $20 to $23/hr. The posting says $23 is a firm cap.
-Shift: Monday through Friday, 9:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., plus every other Saturday. The posting doesn't say which time zone, but you must live in the Eastern or Central time zone. Weekends, holidays, or after hours may be needed.
-Benefits: Health, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k) and pension with a 4% employer contribution, 15 days of PTO, company-paid life and disability insurance, FSA and HSA plans, and 50% off select Purdue and Kaplan courses.
-Equipment Provided: Not stated in the posting. Ask in the interview.
-Felony Friendly?: Case by case
-Drug Test: Required. The pre-employment drug screen includes medical and recreational marijuana.
-Notes: This is a strong-paying, full-time role with a pension, but it's not entry level. Homecare Homebase experience is required, plus a year of insurance verification, authorization, or medical billing. Best for a participant coming from a home health or hospice office. The drug screen includes marijuana, even with a medical card. Training length and camera requirements are not listed.
-Career Pathway: Reasonable inferred path: Insurance Verification & Authorization Coordinator → Senior Authorization Specialist → Intake or Revenue Cycle Team Lead → Revenue Cycle Supervisor. This role builds insurance, authorization, and healthcare revenue cycle skills.
